75fd35db-6b4e-5820-b6ac-925d24a0f117.title: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola with Vertex at the Origin Given a Graph

e-5333.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola with Vertex at the Origin Given a Graph
e-5333.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041337/assets/70ff1c84aa4a9a2adc393fc1dcf684ee0bcf161671b15f9061e2319f5d7e0a39.png)

  

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
e-5333.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that the arms of the parabola open to the left. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(-8,4).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
y^2  = 4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(-8,4),$ we can substitute $x = -8$ and $y = 4$ into the standard equation and solve for $p\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {4}^{2} & =4p(-8) \\ 16 & =-32p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(-\frac{1}{2})x \\ {y}^{2} & =-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the left since $p = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ is negative.

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?

b

c

y2=−92x

decision.explanation: The parabola has vertex (0,0), so y² = kx. Substituting (3,2) gives 4 = 3k, hence k = 4/3. Therefore y² = (4/3)x.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041337/assets/4938d034c766b78e1da1a5bd19f2a12b314f772ca4819cd52d4f1463ff1ae3a4.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
after.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(3,2).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(3,2),$ we can substitute $x=3$ and $y=2$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {2}^{2} & =4p(3) \\ 4 & =12p \\ p & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{3})x \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{4}{3}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{1}{3}$ is positive.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041337/assets/83439b98fff25c021a2713448779167f25a0b9f04dd0d14b115a55f915e3501d.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
after.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(12,6).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(12,6),$ we can substitute $x=12$ and $y=6$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {6}^{2} & =4p(12) \\ 36 & =48p \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{3}{4})x \\ {y}^{2} & =3x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{3}{4}$ is positive.
